{{Short description|Open source software demonstrations}}
[[File:Tangent 1.jpg|thumb|One of the Demonstrations about [[Tangent|surface tangents]]]]The '''Wolfram Demonstrations Project''' is an [[Open source|open-source]] collection of [[Interactive computing|interactive programmes]] called Demonstrations. It is hosted by [[Wolfram Research]]. At its launch, it contained 1300 demonstrations but has grown to over 10,000. The site won a [[Parents' Choice Award]] in 2008.

[[Wolfram Research]]'s staff organizes and edits the Demonstrations, which may be created by any user of [[Wolfram Mathematica|Mathematica]], then freely published<ref>[http://www.scientific-computing.com/education/archives/29 Throwing beanbags in Mathematica 6] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015201652/http://www.scientific-computing.com/education/archives/29 |date=2007-10-15 }}, Scientific Computing, May 17, 2007.</ref> and freely downloaded.

==Technology==
The Demonstrations run in [[Wolfram Mathematica|Mathematica]] 6 or above and in Wolfram [[Computable Document Format|CDF Player]], which is a free modified version of [[Wolfram Mathematica]]<ref>[http://www.maa.org/editorial/mathgames/mathgames_05_02_07.html Math Games] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070504043454/http://www.maa.org/editorial/mathgames/mathgames_05_02_07.html |date=2007-05-04 }} MAA Online, May 1, 2007.</ref> and available for [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[Linux]], and [[macOS]]<ref>[http://www.scientificcomputing.com/Adventures-with-the-Wolfram-Demonstrations-Project.aspx Adventures with the Wolfram Demonstrations Project] John Wass, Scientific Computing</ref> and can operate as a web [[Browser extension|browser plugin]]. Demonstrations can also be embedded into a website.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kaurov |first=Vitaliy |title=Add a Wolfram Demonstration to Your Site in One Easy Step |date=24 April 2012 |url=http://blog.wolfram.com/2012/04/24/add-a-wolfram-demonstration-to-your-site-in-one-easy-step/}}</ref> Each Demonstration page includes a snippet of [[JavaScript]] code in the Share section of the sidebar.

The Demonstrations typically consist of a direct user interface to a graphic or visualization that dynamically responds to user actions. Each Demonstration also has a description of the concept. The website is organized by topic, for example: science,<ref>[http://www.sciencebase.com/science-blog/molecular-wolfram-demonstrations.html Molecular Wolfram Demonstrations] ScienceBase</ref> art, and biology.
